findings.problem: The STU-002 repair removed the manufactured roles. Each interpretation now ends its section on the other texts with a paragraph of bare clauses for the texts it does not use. Lane 2's last three sentences list the feast's three orations, the Sunday's three prayers and the Preface. Lane 3's paragraph lists ten texts (Collect, Secret, Lesson, Alleluia, Communion, Postcommunion, the Sunday's three prayers, the Preface), each with a Latin word, and never says what the interpretation makes of them. Lane 1's last paragraph does the same for the Offertory and the Sunday prayers; its Sicard sentence is a real connection and is not part of this finding. The clauses repeat what the map, the appointed texts and the element settings already give, and 'Either Preface ends with the praise of the angels' appears four times. Nothing in them is false and no role is claimed, and the profile gives a lightly touched text a clause. But gathered at the end of a section, with no bearing on the argument, they serve only to show coverage (guidance/editorial.md, 'Each sentence adds something', 'Say it once'). In lane 3 the bare words abundantiam, salutaria, reficiam, muniri and humanis periculis invite the reader to supply the roles that STU-002 removed. Advisory: the clauses are the ones the earlier required result asked for, they mislead no one, and they cost the reader a paragraph.

State the Preface fact once, in the element settings, and in an interpretation only where the angels matter (lane 1). findings.problem: Four sentences tell the reader that a difficulty is hard, or that a disagreement is real or still stands, before saying what it is. That is performed emphasis, and 'the disagreement stands' names the discipline of keeping a difference rather than simply carrying it (guidance/editorial.md, 'Let emphasis come from content'; 'State the finding, not the process', on prose saying a difference was retained). 40:29-30 ends its paragraph on a turn that the next paragraph's objection already makes. These are isolated instances in different wordings, and the content after each is right.
findings.required_result: Let the content carry the weight and cut the certifying clause. Rewrites: (1) 30:201-204 -> 'Hilary places the rewards in heaven, for those changed by immortality. On his account the Gospel describes chiefly the state the saints now possess; on the others', the life they already lived.' (2) 40:106-109 -> 'The four agree that the fearer lacks nothing that matters, and disagree whether bodily need is included: Basil excludes bodily goods by the apostles' example, and Aquinas meets the same example with the physician.' summary: Cold review of the revised expansive study (main.tex, research edition) of the 1962 F02 All Saints leaf under provider claude. I built it in scratch: 31 letter pages, references settled, no LaTeX warnings, and every research-edition content preflight passes. The appointed-text mode is complete, with the Full PDF label, which agrees with the production plan (no reference-only authorization) and with the reviewed research; the printed Latin agrees with propers/verified.md. Checked at the cited loci in the registered text layers: Chrysostom, Hom. in Matt. 15.4, 15.5, 15.9 and 38.3 (NPNF I.10); Basil, Hom. in Ps. 32 n. 1 and 33 nn. 6-7 (PG 29 Latin); Augustine, Enarr. 32 en. 1 and en. 2 s. 1, 33 s. 2 nn. 14, 15 and 19, and 87 n. 5 (Migne), with Sermons XIX [LXIX] and LXI (NPNF 6); Bede on Apoc 7:1-12 (Marshall); Hilary, In Matt. IV nn. 1-9 (PL 9); Bernard, sermo 1 nn. 9 and 13-15, sermo 2 n. 1 and sermo 5 nn. 2-3 and 5 (PL 183); Aquinas, In Ps. 32 and In Ps. 33 n. 10 (Parma), Super Matt. 5 (Venice) and ST I q. 23 a. 7; Bellarmine on Pss 32-33; Bonaventure on Wis 3:1-3; Schuster pp. 209-211; Fromage on the Introit, Collect, Offertory and Communion; Durandus VII.34; Sicard IX.49; Gregory, Hom. in Ev. 34 n. 11; Cyprian, Ad Fortunatum 11; Victorinus on 7:2-9; Alphonsus, Ninth Consideration; and the Cassiodorus extract in PL 142. Every quotation and attribution checked supports the study's sentence. Difficulty tests. Lane 1: Apoc 7:4 against 7:9, at Bede on 7:4 and 7:9. The study marks the identity of the number and the multitude as its own inference from Bede's two comments, and it holds (pass). Lane 2: the tenses of the beatitudes, at Chrysostom Hom. 15.4-15.5 and Augustine De serm. Dom. I.4.12. Pass, and the STU-005 repair is confirmed. Lane 3: Ps 33:10-11, at Basil n. 7's dilemma of the apostles and Aquinas n. 10's physician. Both inferences are the authors' own and the study teaches the question from Augustine's objector, n. 14 (pass). Not re-read: the Enchiridion (remote bytes only), the image-read Rabanus, Jerome and Hilary XI excerpts, the restricted Leonine Super Matt. text, and the facsimile collation. The eight standing blocking findings STU-001 to STU-008 are repaired and the advisories STU-009 to STU-012 are cleared. No blocking defect remains. Three new advisories record residual coverage lists (STU-013), certifying lead-ins (STU-014) and small precision points (STU-015). This dispatch contributed the independent cold review of the revised expansive study, with source checks at about thirty cited loci.
